business_scope.primary_industry_name: Virtual Expense Card Issuing and Spend Management Controls

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Vanuatu (Unitary National Jurisdiction; regulatory hub: Port Vila; no sub-state or provincial tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (English common law foundation, French civil law influence, and unregistered Melanesian customary law; International Company law modelled on the BVI-style International Business Companies framework)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus - Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (entered into force 13 December 2020; trade and investment facilitation)
OECD Global Forum Tax Information Exchange Agreements (no comprehensive double-tax-agreement network with major capital-exporting states)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act [Cap. 222] (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2014); Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act No. 7 of 2020; Financial Intelligence Unit Act No. 2 of 2020; Vanuatu Financial Services Commission Act 1999 (as amended); VFSC AML/CFT Rules and Guidance Notes; National Payment System Act 2019 (authorisation covering payment instruments and card-related activities).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (share register and beneficial-ownership data are confidential; VFSC and Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit obtain and supervise UBO declarations through licensed registered agents; nominee arrangements must be disclosed to the regulator and do not confer statutory secrecy)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Vanuatu International Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission - International Companies Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Vanuatu is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention 1961): notarisation in Vanuatu, authentication by the Vanuatu Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade (MFAT), then legalisation by the destination-country consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association of the International Company (constitutional charter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Vanuatu licensed registered agent (lodged with VFSC and executed by incorporating shareholder and director)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarisation, MFAT authentication, destination-consulate legalisation)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency (listing directors, secretary, and beneficial owners)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Vanuatu licensed registered agent, countersigned by VFSC where required
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarisation, MFAT authentication, destination-consulate legalisation)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised copy of passport and Proof of Identity affidavit of each director, shareholder, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the Republic of Vanuatu
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (notarisation, MFAT authentication, destination-consulate legalisation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all incorporators, directors, UBOs, registered-agent client introducers, and card-program counterparties against: (i) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) OFAC SDN and OFAC sectoral lists (mandatory given USD settlement on Mastercard Network and Visa Direct rails); (iii) EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions; (iv) FATF/APG high-risk and monitored jurisdictions; (v) Vanuatu domestic PEP database, including Bislama-name aliases; and (vi) adverse-media and negative-news data sets. Continuous 24-hour re-screening is required under VFSC AML/CFT Rules; discrepancies, hits, or suspicious activity must be escalated to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit by suspicious-transaction report.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission - International Companies Registry online name-reservation portal (vfsc.vu e-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must comprise only Latin-script (Roman alphabet) characters in the English or French language; Bislama and other foreign-language names are accepted solely in Romanised transliteration. The statutory suffix must appear as an English or French corporate-form indicator (e.g., 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'S.A.R.L.'). No national-script, pictorial, or non-Latin characters are accepted by the registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of the International Companies Registry within 14 business days, identifying the distinguishing elements between the proposed name and the conflicting entry and attaching any prior ministerial or sectoral approval obtained for sensitive tokens. Simultaneously, two alternate names may be reserved to protect the incorporation timetable. Where reconsideration is declined, the applicant may present an administrative appeal to the VFSC Board of Appeal within 21 business days of declination; the Board decides on statutory undesirability, phonetic similarity, and public-policy grounds. A name reservation may be extended once by 30 days upon payment of the statutory extension tariff; final judicial review lies with the Supreme Court of Vanuatu.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is insufficient to satisfy the statutory registered-office obligation under the International Companies Act: every International Company must maintain a physical registered office in Vanuatu through a licensed registered agent. For this ISIC 6619 / NAICS 522320 card-issuer project, a virtual address is unacceptable as the sole substance measure at the financial-licence application stage; VFSC will require a genuine operational footprint, including governance, compliance officers, and accountable executives, proportionate to the High_Risk_Special_License classification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Model estimate for the first licensed operating year: 35% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by VFSC or the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu owing to the high-risk fintech classification. Pre-licensing period risk: below 10%. Inspectors hold statutory power to examine registered-office records, UBO files, AML systems, and card-program evidence without notice.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1992 (Cap. 222) of Vanuatu, ss. 11-16 (Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles, Name, Registered Office and Registered Agent), read with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (Fees) Regulations and the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorism Financing Act 2024 (No. 25 of 2024)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — Registry of International Companies, Port Vila, Vanuatu
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association executed by all subscribers and filed with the Registrar of International Companies under s. 11 of the International Companies Act 1992
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum authorized or paid-up capital is prescribed for a Vanuatu International Company; a single no-par-value share may be issued on incorporation and subscription proceeds are held by the Registered Agent, with no statutory escrow account requirement under the IC Act 1992
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Memorandum and Articles of Association be adopted, and the initial shares be subscribed and allotted to the founding member against the agreed consideration; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the Company be situated at the Registered Agent's address in Port Vila, and the Registered Agent be authorized to file statutory notices and maintain the statutory registers; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the persons named in the appointment schedule be appointed as first Director, Secretary, and Compliance Officer, each to hold office until removed; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the Directors be authorized to open bank accounts, appoint auditors, and apply to the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission for all licenses required for virtual card issuance and payment services.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Engagement of Licensed Registered Agent and Execution of Engagement Letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC-licensed Registered Agent (private sector, supervised by the VFSC Registry of International Companies)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the registered agent engagement and indemnity letter; the Agent verifies each shareholder's and director's identity under the VFI KYC rules; prepare the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association, and establish the corporate file for the Company.
required_dossiers: KYC/DD form for each beneficial owner
Certified passport copy and proof of residential address for each director and shareholder
Banker's reference (original) for each director and shareholder
Certificate of incorporation and good standing of any corporate shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Agent determines that the ownership or reputational profile is materially deficient, the applicant may substitute principals or provide enhanced due diligence evidence; no registry filing is affected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation with the Registry of International Companies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Registry of International Companies (online filing through the licensed Registered Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent lodges a name reservation request with up to three proposed names; the name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing company and must not imply a restricted activity (banking, insurance, trust) absent a licence; the chosen name must carry an acceptable suffix such as 'Limited'.
required_dossiers: Power to represent the applicant (agent's authority)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refused or conditionally accepted name may be re-submitted with alternative names on the same reservation; VFSC issues a formal name objection notice permitting argument or substitution within 14 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Filing of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Registry of International Companies, Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All subscribers execute the Memorandum and Articles before a notary or by authorized signatory; the Registered Agent files the signed instrument with the Registry together with prescribed consent forms and pays the registration fee on behalf of the Company.
required_dossiers: Signed Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Registrar may issue a requisition or correction notice for formal defects; the Agent files corrected documents within 14 days of notice without loss of the original submission date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Statutory Registration Fee and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: VFSC Registry of International Companies, Port Vila
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory review, the VFSC collects the government registration fee (USD 350 standard minimum tier) and issues a Certificate of Incorporation in the name of the International Company; the effective date is the date shown on the Certificate.
required_dossiers: VFSC fee invoice and payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If issuance is delayed, the Agent files a status inquiry with the Registry; typographical errors in the Certificate are cured by a formal Request for Correction accompanied by the original Certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Passing of First Board Resolution and Appointment of Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company, convened by the Registered Agent or Company Secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The first Director convenes a board meeting or passes a unanimous written resolution adopting the pro-forma first board resolution; the resolution fixes the initial share allotment, adopts the registered office and Agent, appoints the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, and authorizes corporate bank account opening and VFSC licensing submissions.
required_dossiers: Pro-forma first board resolution (minutes or written resolution)
Consent-to-act forms of the Secretary and Compliance Officer
Register of Directors and Register of Members
Applicant identification for bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any appointed person declines office, the Board passes a supplementary resolution naming a replacement officer; the minutes are amended by Board consent before filing into the corporate records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Statutory Registers, Seal and Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent for records and the first Director for certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following incorporation, the Company instructs the Registered Agent to maintain the statutory registers (members, directors and charges), issues the share certificate to the founding member, adopts a common seal if desired, and prepares the AML/CFT compliance manual with the VFI where the Company commences regulated card-issuing activity.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Inaccuracies in the registers are rectified by Board resolution followed by an updated register entry; records are produced to the VFSC upon request within three business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) — Licensing and Compliance Department, read with the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu payment systems clearance where card scheme participation requires settlement in Vanuatu
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: VFSC Financial Services Authorisation for Payment Services and Virtual Card Issuing (non-bank electronic money and card scheme participant), conditioned upon AML/CFT programme approval by the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (VFI)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation (DEPC), Ministry of Climate Change, Vanuatu
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based financial activity with no physical manufacturing plant, no industrial discharges and no land disturbance; no EIA study or registration certificate is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to the licensed activity; if a local office is opened in Port Vila, routine municipal solid waste disposal must comply with the Waste Management Regulations 2020; no industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds are triggered by virtual card issuance operations

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification for office premises issued by the Vanuatu Police Fire Service / National Disaster Management Office on annual inspection; structural load clearance for any office tenancy under the Building Act 2017; occupational workplace health and safety clearance under the Employment Act 2008 (Cap 160) and associated regulations; additional cyber-risk and data residency compliance under the Vanuatu Data Protection Act 2024 where personal data of Vanuatu residents is processed

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Vanuatu Customs and Inland Revenue Department, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management; portal: https://customs.invanuatu.gov.vu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign or offshore entity must submit the VAT registration application (Form VAT-1) together with certified constitutional documents, proof of physical or registered address, VFSC registration certificate (for International Companies), and bank account details. The application is filed with the Comptroller of Customs and Inland Revenue. An International Company formed under the International Companies Act is exempt from national income tax and is not ordinarily required to obtain a TIN; however, it must maintain its VFSC registration number and may optionally obtain a VAT ID only if it carries on nonexempt taxable activities in Vanuatu, which is inconsistent with the offshore restriction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vanuatu has no check-the-box election. International Companies automatically receive a statutory tax exemption under the International Companies Act, unless they violate the offshore activity restriction and become subject to domestic VAT. There are no hybrid mismatch elections because Vanuatu imposes no income tax on offshore entities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VUV 5,000,000 (Vanuatu Vatu) of taxable supplies in any 12-month consecutive period; offshore International Companies providing no domestic taxable supplies are not registrable
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API-based e-reporting, digital stamping, or continuous invoice-control mandate is in force. VAT-registered businesses must issue compliant paper or electronic VAT invoices. Export declarations are processed through the ASYCUDA World customs administration system without a mandatory third-party fiscal clearance API.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A VAT-registered supplier may zero-rate exports of goods where the goods are physically exported outside Vanuatu within the prescribed period, transport services connected with those exports, and supplies of services to a non-resident where the benefit of the services occurs wholly outside Vanuatu. An International Company with the restricted offshore business model is not a VAT-registered trader and therefore cannot practically claim input VAT refunds; any incidental export-like supply would fall under the tax-exempt offshore status rather than the VAT zero-rating mechanism.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or erroneous claims of export zero-rating trigger retrospective assessments, with the full VAT deducted as input credit clawed back plus late-payment penalties and interest. Making a false declaration to the Customs authority or VAT administration constitutes an offence punishable by monetary penalties up to three times the tax evaded and, for serious cases, imprisonment. An International Company that attempts to use zero-rating while breaching the offshore restriction risks loss of the statutory tax-exempt status, retroactive taxation, and VFSC regulatory sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV) - central bank and exchange-control authority; Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) - delegated regulator for Financial Dealers Licensing Act [Cap 228] and non-bank financial supervision; National Payment System Act oversight with RBV.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vanuatu Vatu (VUV) is administered against a trade-weighted basket of the AUD, USD and SDR. Vanuatu observes current-account convertibility and IMF Article VIII obligations; current payments for trade, services, dividends and interest are unrestricted. Capital-account operations are liberalized but resident entities may need RBV approval or reporting under the Exchange Control Act [Cap 65]; a VFSC-registered International Company (IC) is non-resident and statutorily exempt from exchange-control approval, removing remittance, dividend and capital-repatriation hurdles provided AML/KYC conditions are satisfied.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters must offer all foreign currency export proceeds to an RBV-authorized dealer within 3 months of the entitlement date and convert 100% unless an RBV exemption is granted. The Exchange Control Act excludes International Companies from the resident definition, so the VU IC may retain export, card-interchange and programme-fee proceeds in VUV or any permitted foreign currency account without surrender or mandatory conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Settlement Account (USD/VUV); Capital Escrow Account for licensed programme
Multi-currency Operational Account; segregated Cardholder Reserve Account
Corporate Operational Account; FX hedging margin account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW-MEDIUM. Vanuatu has no electronic-money institution (EMI) licensing regime and no passporting for foreign EMIs; taking VUV deposits would require a banking licence under the Banking Act [Cap 112]. Offshore EMIs can act only as non-deposit-taking card programme managers/processors under a VFSC-reviewed servicer due-diligence file and a written programme-management agreement, with settlement accounts held at, or sub-accounted through, an RBV-authorized domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is not prohibited by the Vanuatu AML/CFT framework, but tier-1 banks in practice require a mandatory compliance interview; for a High-Risk_Special_License virtual-card issuer, at least one director/authorized signatory must attend the Port Vila branch interview in person, or the bank may permit two-way video KYC only with a VFSC-licensed registered agent certifying the principal under a trusted-introducer arrangement, plus certified board resolutions and UBO verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-face-to-face onboarding of a newly incorporated non-resident IC with no operating history and no audited financial statements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: VFSC certificate of incorporation and good standing; Central Beneficial Ownership Register extract; notarized statutory declaration of non-residence by each director/UBO; two or three bank references from existing professional banks; source-of-funds bundle (share subscription agreements, investor KYC, programme sponsor commitment); registered-agent letter under the International Companies Act confirming domicile and call-back verification.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency cross-border card disbursements and multi-currency settlement through third-party processors or offshore EMIs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved AML/CFT compliance manual and independent compliance audit opinion; transaction-monitoring and sanctions-screening configuration (UN, OFAC, EU, VFIU watchlists); Visa/Mastercard sponsoring-principal approval letter; programme-manager and processor agreements; client-funds segregation undertaking; audit-rights clause in favour of the domestic settlement bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-tax offshore status and absence of physical office/tax residence triggering shell-company or BEPS red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: VFSC tax-exemption certificate issued under the International Companies Act; VFSC-licensed registered-office evidence; minutes of real board/treasury decisions; CRS and economic-substance self-certification; annual corporate return and audited or reviewed financial statements confirming substance proportionate to the card-issuing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-card volume exposed to high-risk merchant verticals (gambling, foreign exchange brokerages, digital assets)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Merchant vertical policy prohibiting or strictly limiting restricted categories; cardholder onboarding and velocity-limit documentation; automated daily limit and country-blocking parameters; internal escalation register and Suspicious Transaction Report filing record with the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit; network compliance attestation and scheme-audit certificate.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital is routed by SWIFT MT103 from the parent/shareholder to the VU IC account at an RBV-authorized bank. Field 70 must carry ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity injection) or 'INTE' (intercompany loan) with the narrative 'Shareholder capital contribution / license capital - International Company'. The receiving bank verifies the VFSC certificate, tax-exemption certificate and beneficial-ownership extract before crediting; no RBV exchange-control permit applies to the non-resident IC, but the receipt must be recorded in the annual VFSC IC return and in any RBV aggregate reporting when a resident counterparty is involved.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Card-network settlements clear through Mastercard Clearing Management System (CMS) and Visa Base II/COMET with funding by SWIFT MT103 and MT202 COV cover transfers to the network's settlement bank; cardholder and merchant disbursements use MT103 with ISO purpose codes 'CCRD' or 'TRAD'; documentary trade payments are supported by Commercial Letters of Credit issued via SWIFT MT700/MT710 series under UCP 600; domestic VUV legs settle through the RBV-operated RTGS (Port Vila) and National Payment System on a T+0/T+1 daylight basis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright VUV/USD or VUV/AUD foreign-exchange forward with an RBV-authorized dealer for genuine card-settlement exposure
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on VUV/USD where offshore VUV deliverability is unavailable, transacted through Port Vila authorized dealers or Singapore NDF desks with tenor up to 12 months

Cross-currency swap (VUV/USD or VUV/AUD) matched to the rolling settlement liabilities of the card programme, documented under an ISDA form and reported to the RBV as a financial-dealer derivative transaction under the Financial Dealers Licensing Act [Cap 228]

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Return and Government License Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC), Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after each incorporation anniversary; renewal fee payable by 30 June annually (or anniversary date per agent contract)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late penalty of VUV 10,000 (approx. USD 85) plus VUV 1,000 per day; persistent failure for 3 months may lead to administrative strike-off and loss of limited liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and Annual Compliance Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) Financial Dealers Licensing Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of financial year end; most entities aligned to 31 December, filing due 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License suspension and monetary penalty up to VUV 1,000,000 (approx. USD 8,500); non-compliance may trigger license revocation and entity strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) Filing and Risk Assessment Review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit (VFIU) via VFSC
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March or per AML/CFT license conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to VUV 500,000 (approx. USD 4,200); repeated non-compliance leads to criminal sanctions and license revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the International Companies Act, audit is not mandatory for standard ICs solely based on turnover or asset thresholds; however, any holder of a financial dealer license for virtual card issuing must appoint an independent auditor and file audited financial statements annually.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted for international companies; VFSC licenses require IFRS-compliant financial statements in English.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must obtain and retain the beneficial ownership register under the Companies (International Company) Regulations and AML/CFT laws. On every share transfer, the register is updated and the registered agent must make an annual confirmation to VFSC that the UBO information is current; a signed declaration of beneficial ownership is required from directors within 30 days of any change.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% - Vanuatu does not levy corporate income tax on International Companies
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions are available because the base corporate income tax rate is 0%. International Companies are tax-exempt outside the scope of Vanuatu income tax legislation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: No CIT return is required. Vanuatu International Companies file an annual return under the International Companies Act Cap. 222 through the VFSC e-Services portal or the licensed registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is due within six months after the anniversary of the company's registration date. Failure to file may trigger VFSC administrative strike-off proceedings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the International Company and the VFSC registration number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the exact legal name and registration number from the certificate. No tax identification number is required because International Companies are not registered for corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical registered office address in Vanuatu and name of the Vanuatu-licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must appoint a Vanuatu-licensed registered agent. The registered office may not be a bare letterbox; a physical address and agent in Vanuatu are mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names, addresses, and identification particulars of all directors and the company secretary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Vanuatu IC law permits non-resident directors. At least one director and, where required, a secretary must be named; the registered agent fulfils the resident representative function.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered shareholder names, share classes, percentage holdings, and beneficial ownership declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Bearer shares are prohibited. Non-resident shareholders must provide passport, proof of address, and source-of-funds documentation for AML/CDD purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Signed registered-agent declaration that the company is in compliance with the International Companies Act and has paid the annual fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No taxable profit, revenue, or balance-sheet values are reported because the IC has no CIT filing obligation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts a VFSC penalty fee. Continuing failure for more than six months may result in strike-off from the Register, asset freezing side-effects, and costly restoration procedures. False statements in the annual return are criminal offences punishable by fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Vanuatu does not impose dividend withholding tax on outbound distributions from an International Company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not applicable under domestic law. Because Vanuatu imposes no withholding tax, no DTA relief claim is necessary. If a foreign tax authority requires proof of Vanuatu tax status, the IC may obtain a Certificate of Incumbency and/or tax status certificate through the VFSC registered agent. Vanuatu does not issue a standard TRC in respect of income that is not within its tax jurisdiction.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% for outbound royalties and debt interest. Treaty rate: Not applicable - Vanuatu's limited tax agreements are principally for information exchange and do not reduce any domestic withholding rate because no positive withholding rate exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable - Vanuatu has no transfer-pricing legislation, no arm's-length documentation thresholds, and no local-file/master-file rules for International Companies.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu International Companies are subject to economic substance expectations under the VFSC licensing framework and related Company/ESR rules. A B2B virtual card issuer must maintain real economic presence in Vanuatu - including local physical office, eligible decision-makers, board minutes, employment substance, and activity consistent with the VFSC financial services licence. Passive letterbox arrangements are not tolerated in licensed financial services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Misuse of Tax-Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Falsely representing to foreign tax authorities that the Vanuatu IC has paid corporate income tax or issuing invoices that misstate the IC's tax-exempt status to disguise taxable revenue booked in another jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Vanuatu law and the International Companies Act Cap. 222, with statutory fines up to VT 10,000,000, deregistration of the IC, confiscation order, and permanent prohibition from holding a VFSC licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the corporate veil where the IC is a mere instrument of fraud. Directors are exposed to civil restitution to affected stakeholders, travel bans, disqualification from management, and imprisonment upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Virtual Card Issuance / Banking Activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing corporate virtual cards or operating Visa/Mastercard payment rails without a valid VFSC financial services licence, or exceeding the scope of the licence through deposit-taking or customer third-party fund handling.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlicensed conduct triggers VFSC enforcement action, including immediate licence suspension, civil penalties, freezing orders, forced remediation, and referral to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit for money-laundering and terrorist-financing investigation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers face personal criminal liability, director-ban orders, and travel bans. Personal restitution liability attaches where funds of cardholders or merchants were mishandled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing B2B virtual cards without adequate customer due diligence, beneficial-ownership verification, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, or suspicious-transaction reporting, particularly for high-risk cross-border payment flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under anti-money-laundering legislation and VFSC rules, failure to maintain required AML controls attracts monetary penalties, revocation of the VFSC licence, and designation as a prohibited person for financial services. Regulators may also impose enhanced supervision costs on the institution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly permit AML failures are individually liable for civil penalties and criminal prosecution; imprisonment is available for aggravated non-compliance. Personal assets may be subject to civil forfeiture in successful enforcement proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a pure shell - no Vanuatu physical office, no on-island management, no substantive board activity, and no commensurate staffing - while obtaining a VFSC licence and promoting VU tax/financial advantages to foreign clients.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VFSC may impose economic-substance penalties, strike the IC off the Register, and transmit adverse notices to foreign tax authorities and international regulators. The company can be forced into compulsory winding-up.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who execute sham substance arrangements face personal fines, disqualification orders, travel bans, and civil liability for regulatory costs and client losses. The corporate veil will be disregarded where substance was artificially manufactured to shield another jurisdiction's taxable business.
